newsitem.title: USA: Dow zigzags higher, capping week-long bounce.
newsitem.headline: Dow zigzags higher, capping week-long bounce.

text.p: Wall Street stocks whipsawed higher on Friday, capping a furious week that saw the Dow industrials surge more than 300 points.

The Dow rose 45 points to close unofficially at 6704 after a choppy session dominated by options expiration activity. The Nasdaq Composite also finished higher, powered by Microsoft Corp, which soared a day after the company reported very strong third quarter earnings.
With the gains, the Dow has now reversed almost half of its nearly 10 percent decline between mid-March and mid-April.
But even as the Dow continued to undo the damage from its month-long slide, analysts were reluctant to predict clear sailing for stocks.

"We saw some good bargain hunting this week, but overall the market was quite mixed," said Eugene Peroni, chief technical analyst with Janney, Montgomery Scott. "I would view this week as an impressive reaction to an oversold market."

Analysts pointed to the relatively strong showings by sectors typically viewed as defensive investments, such as oil and consumer products companies, as evidence of a market still tentative after its recent shelling.
The Dow's top gaining stocks were Philip Morris Cos Inc which gained 2-5/8 to 44-1/4 and Exxon Corp, up two to 53-1/2.

"The rally has been fairly narrow, which disturbs us a bit," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker. "This market has to rotate and the cyclicals are going to have to emerge as leadership for this market to get its next leg up."
The narrowness of the rally was most evident among Nasdaq stocks, which managed only modest gains despite Microsoft's stellar 9-1/2 point rally to 107-5/8.
Advancing issues outnumbered declining issues by a roughly five-to-three margin on the New York Stock Exchange but on Nasdaq winners and losers ran in a dead heat.

"Point for point, the statistics may show this was one of the best weeks for some of the averages," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "But this wasn't a case where a rising tide lifted all the ships."
Indeed, beyond Microsoft, the performance by even top technology names was unimpressive, with Intel Corp off 7/8 to 137-1/8 and Cisco Systems Inc down 1-1/8 to 48-3/8.
The flow of major earnings releases slowed to a trickle today, but even so, investors had plenty to keep them occupied.
Hershey Foods Corp jumped 1-1/2 to 52-7/8 after the company's first quarter earnings matched Wall Street estimates.

Silicon Graphics Inc skidded 4-1/8 to 12-7/8. Several investment firms downgraded the shares today, a day after the graphics systems company reported fiscal third quarter earnings sharply below analysts' forecasts.
Russell Corp tumbled 8-1/2 to 27-1/4 after the leisure and athletic apparel maker company reported lower than expected first quarter earnings.
The S&P 500 index rose 4.57 points to 766.34.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 5.50 points to 1222.57.
